claims.quote_span: We present 2241 exoplanet candidates identified with data from the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) during its two-year prime mission.
claims.text: The TESS Objects of Interest (TOI) Catalog is the source catalog for the candidates whose dispositions (CP, FP, PC, APC) the T1 snapshot check compares. The prime-mission release listed 2241 candidates. This is background context only. It does not show that archive values separate resolved TOIs from unresolved ones.

claims.quote_span: We list these candidates in the TESS Objects of Interest (TOI) Catalog, which includes both new planet candidates found by TESS and previously-known planets recovered by TESS observations.
claims.text: The TOI Catalog includes both new TESS planet candidates and previously known planets that TESS recovered. A snapshot comparison should therefore not assume that every CP disposition came from TESS-only vetting.

claims.quote_span: The Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) will search for planets transiting bright and nearby stars.
claims.text: TESS is a transit survey of bright, nearby stars. This mission design shapes which stellar and transit parameters appear in the archive values used for the T1 check.

payload.search_scope: Run live-exo-8. I ran no live literature search; no search tool was available in this session. I checked the three supplied EVIDENCE_ADDED claims and added prior art I know from memory. The evidence covers only the source catalog (Guerrero et al. 2021 TOI Catalog) and the mission design (Ricker et al. 2015). None of it tests whether archive features separate resolved TOIs (CP/FP) from unresolved ones (PC/APC). The closest work I know is machine-learning classification of transit candidates by planet versus false-positive disposition: Shallue & Vanderburg 2018 on Kepler, Yu et al. 2019 on TESS, and Armstrong et al. 2021 on planet validation. That makes it plausible that archive features carry disposition-related signal. However, those papers classify planets against false positives, not resolved against unresolved status, and they mostly use light curves rather than snapshot archive tabular values. I found no exact match, but my search was not exhaustive, so I am not labelling this NOVEL. A follow-up should search ADS and arXiv for 'TOI disposition prediction catalog features' and for work on how long TOIs stay in PC status.

payload.summary: Preliminary, AI-generated. T1 shift check on a single catalog snapshot (NASA Exoplanet Archive TOI table, 2026-10-04T09:37:14Z, sha256:485a05d6f94c; 7427 TOIs, 7143 hosts, 39 features; 2127 resolved CP/FP vs 5300 unresolved PC/APC). The primary logistic regression, excluding timestamps and grouped by host, gave out-of-fold ROC AUC 0.762 (95% cluster-bootstrap CI 0.750-0.774, 200 replicates). This SUPPORTS H1's directional prediction (prior predicted 0.70 +/- 0.10). The arm with timestamps gave AUC 0.766 (0.755-0.775). This is snapshot separability, not vetting accuracy, causality, or generalization. The permutation test was skipped. Novelty is UNCERTAIN: the referee ran no live search. REPLAN: preregister host-disjoint, later-snapshot evaluation with ablations of timestamps and features potentially downstream of disposition.
